title: Tail-aware KV prefetch playbook and golden trace dataset for long-context regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: produce an operational playbook and a validated "golden trace" dataset to safely enable tail-aware KV prefetching and per-model version pin recommendations for long-context model variants. The deliverable bundle: (1) a 20–30 example golden_trace_v1.s3 artifact covering diverse sequence distributions and adversarial tails, (2) an automated validation suite that runs in CI and on staging to check warmup success, memory delta, and regression windows, and (3) a documented playbook for oncall + release engineers describing gating, rollback, and observability checks.
acceptance_criteria: Golden trace set (>= 20 traces) uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/golden_traces/golden_trace_v1.tar.gz
CI step `kvcache-prefetch-validate` passes against runtime-staging with zero regressed templates (thresholds defined below)
Playbook doc published (Confluence) with clear rollback steps and alert thresholds
Automated publication pipeline tags model versions with `tail-aware-prefetch:eligible` only if all checks pass
validation_thresholds: cold_start_token_overhead <= 50ms per 256 tokens on p3.2xlarge equivalent
memory_delta <= +10% for pinned KV retention configuration
no model-level output-quality regressions above 0.5% on eval promptset
notes: 2025-01-12: Kickoff with runtime, infra, and eval teams. Agreed scope: golden traces must include multi-turn code-reasoning, retrieval-augmented chat, and long-document summarization flows.
2025-01-21: Decided to avoid optimistic aggressive prefetching for small enterprise tenants due to memory pressure — per-tenant caps will be enforced.

2025-01-28: Initial synthetic adversarial traces created by Research (artifact: s3://redwood-experiments/adversarial_traces/adv_v2.tar.gz). These exposed a regression pattern: prefetch staleness when KV retention window shorter than expected in encode-heavy chains.
2025-02-05: Implemented deterministic warmstart replay harness (PR listed below) to reproduce warmup failures locally. Helps reduce flakiness in CI.
2025-02-11: Follow-up: scheduler trade-off analysis attached. We prefer conservative pinning for models with high KV mutation rate; recommend gradual rollouts with canary traffic at 2% increments.
decisions: Use bucketed sequence distributions instead of single quantile heuristics: maintains stability across heterogeneous workloads.
Publish `tail-aware-prefetch` only when warmup_success_rate >= 98% and memory_delta <= +10%: prioritized reliability over aggressive cost savings.
Gold traces will include both real customer-scrubbed sessions and synthetic adversarial flows; synthetic traces must be labeled and kept separate for auditability.
Pinning policy will prefer model-variant affinity (same quantization/layout) rather than strict version equality to minimize cold starts when binary-compatible variants exist.
tradeoffs: Aggressive prefetch reduces per-token latency for tail sequences but increases memory and risk of stale KV entries that can degrade model quality.
Conservative gating slows feature rollout and may increase tail latency initially, but minimizes rollback events and customer-facing regressions.
Per-tenant caps reduce blast radius but add complexity to autoscaler and billing reconciliation.
runbook: Step 1: Trigger CI `kvcache-prefetch-validate` job with target model/version and golden_trace_v1 artifact
Step 2: Inspect grafana panels: warmup_success_rate, memory_delta, tail_latency buckets
Step 3: If any threshold fails, abort publish and attach failed warmup trace to ticket; notify oncall and research for triage
Step 4: Canary rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 4h observation windows. Stop or rollback on >0.5% QA regression or >5% increase in p95 tail latency
Step 5: After 24h at 100%, mark model version `tail-aware-prefetch:eligible` and publish profile metadata

Finish CI job and add flakiness detection (deadline 2025-02-14). Action: Infra team to add retry/exponential backoff for ephemeral failures.
